unmergedDoubts.whyNotMerged: MERGED, but recording that the merge rests on a shared invariant, not a shared shape: ih hides by marker sets the render pass consults (shadowedSeqs / removedSeqs / rewind windows) while dsh hides by a positional surfaceOp replace carrying sourceEventSeqs. Both keep the durable log untouched and treat the model-visible surface as a projection, so I judged them the same capability; the naming difference ('shadow projection' vs 'surface replace') is exactly the artifact the brief warns about. A reviewer who wants the marker-set/positional-replace split preserved should split row g1, and pre-sampling-compaction-with-provider-routing would then have to move out of it as well.

MERGED into g1 on the invariant 'compaction must never write a new history in place — it publishes a checkpoint plus a replacement history and keeps the original events', which codex states verbatim. Doubt kept because codex's row is also the only carrier of pre-sampling TIMING (run_pre_sampling_compact at the head of run_turn) and of provider routing to remote/server-side compaction, and neither of those is part of the append-only projection capability. If timing deserves its own row, codex's mechanism has to leave g1 and g1 shrinks to ih + dsh.

Left separate. All three end with the model seeing less, but by three different mechanisms: append-only shadowing of a durable log (ih), an optional snip/collapse layer whose modules are null in the shipped bundle (cc-custom), and a full rebuild of fresh history with recoverability supplied by a transcript pointer rather than by the log (grok). Merging them would have claimed a common design that only ih and dsh actually share.

Four injection triggers, four rows anchored on four different surfaces. Time and tmux are per-step durable context snapshots with rate limiting; plan-mode reminders are synthetic parts mutated onto the last user message; the file-reference seam is a cancellable UI picker with no production caller in the host core. g26 very deliberately pairs two of them (dsh file-reference-seam + opencode plan-mode-reminders) as a cross-source row under the 'synthetic fragment in the user message' idea, and I am not confident that pairing is not itself an over-merge — it is the weakest merge in this file.
